html:
Bangkok became the capital of Siam in 1782, when King Rama I, founder of the Chakri dynasty that still reigns, moved across the Chao Phraya River from Thonburi.

He had served under Taksin, who had restored Siam after the fall of Ayutthaya and was overthrown in 1782. Rama I built the Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaew for the Emerald Buddha on an island ringed by canals, copying Ayutthaya's plan.

Bangkok grew as a port, with a large Chinese community trading rice and sugar. After the Bowring Treaty of 1855 it opened to Western trade, and in the 20th century it became one of Asia's great cities.
sum: Bangkok became the capital of Siam in 1782, when King Rama I, founder of the Chakri dynasty that still reigns, moved across the Chao Phraya River from Thonburi.
